historical_reviews.deepseek: Does not analyze the remote register read or its target identity.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Adds access risk but does not prove bus0 is HMC I2C-3,0x11 is FPGA2, or what the returned bytes mean.
historical_reviews.related_cases: Row131 uses the identical register tuple on bus3 for FPGA1. The bus number, FPGA instance and HMC controller are the test's differentiators and require independent evidence.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Review as a gated HMC functional register read with explicit FPGA2 identity, decoder and controller-specific telemetry.

original_test_intent: Verify communication from HMC I2C-3 to FPGA2 through HMC bus0 by reading a defined FPGA2 register and validating the three-byte reply and path-specific error state.
original_method: Map HMC I2C-3 to bus0 and FPGA2 to address0x11; confirm register0x0400 is a safe read target; record ownership and HMC/FPGA2 error baseline; issue one bounded combined pointer-write/read; decode its three bytes for the installed FPGA2 firmware; compare error counters/logs and verify management health.
manual_activity: HMC/FPGA owner supplies the bus0/controller/FPGA2 map, register definition, expected bytes, ownership and recovery. Physical probing/photos are outside the stated method unless separately approved.
required_inputs: PID1114953 mapping of HMC I2C-3 to Linux bus0 and FPGA2 address0x11
Expected three-byte field values/masks and endian interpretation
Confirmation the write phase only positions a read pointer
HMC bus0 driver/daemon owner and raw-access window
Timeout/NACK/retry criteria, path-specific error counters and recovery
safety_requirements: Do not substitute FPGA1/bus3 mapping or results
Prove0x11 identity and0x0400 non-mutating semantics before raw access
Avoid concurrent access with HMC driver or management service
Run one bounded request and preserve the first failure rather than retrying automatically
Abort on wrong response length, invalid field, NACK, timeout, arbitration loss, stuck bus or HMC/FPGA2 health regression
agent_execution_scope: Collect HMC/FPGA2 identity, topology, bus owner and error baseline
After approval, execute the exact single combined read and decode its reply
Do not probe/solder, scan or write other registers, infer FPGA instance, reset HMC/FPGA, retry automatically or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve register0x0400 semantics and expected three-byte decoder
Approve ownership, timeout/abort, recovery and evidence thresholds
Review transaction plus path-specific telemetry and issue verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Incorrect physical-only substitution; the source gives a precise remotely runnable HMC transaction.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After identity/protocol approval, retain `i2ctransfer -y 0 w2@0x11 0x04 0x00 r3` as one bounded combined read; capture stdout/stderr, exit status, latency and decoded FPGA2 fields.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: HMC bus0, address0x11, register bytes0x04/0x00, r3, HMC I2C-3, FPGA2, PID1114953 and 15/5-minute scope are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use one approved controller-specific register read and correlate decoded FPGA2 response with HMC I2C-3 error telemetry.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds precise identity, semantics and acceptance evidence while rejecting an unsupported manual physical test.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A response at0x11 is insufficient without proving that bus0 is HMC I2C-3 and the responder is FPGA2; FPGA1/bus3 results are non-equivalent.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Misinterpreting the pointer write can alter FPGA state, and automatic controller retries can hide intermittent bus faults; digital response does not measure signal integrity.

project_override_considerations: Wistron I2C policy requires platform-management controller, bus, address, protocol, expected response and recovery. HMC bus0 must be explicitly mapped to logical I2C-3.
expected_evidence: PID mapping for HMC I2C-3/bus0/FPGA2 address0x11
HMC and FPGA2 hardware/firmware identities plus bus ownership baseline
Vendor register0x0400 definition and expected three-byte decoder
Timestamped exact transaction with stdout/stderr, exit code, latency and decoded field comparison
Pre/post HMC I2C-3 and FPGA2 error/status telemetry
Post-read management health and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source omits the logical-to-Linux bus map,0x11 FPGA2 identity, register0x0400 semantics and expected r3 value. Both prior reviews additionally impose physical probing that the source does not request.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The functional purpose and precise candidate request are understood; standard owner-supplied mapping/decoder/approval can make it executable, so it is RPUC.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row133 Wistron-HW Robust-00011-V002: provide PID1114953 mapping from HMC I2C-3 to bus0 and FPGA2 at0x11, define register0x0400 combined-read safety and expected three-byte decoder, ownership/exclusive access, timeout/NACK/retry criteria, HMC I2C-3/FPGA2 telemetry and recovery. Confirm physical probing/photos are not core acceptance unless separately scoped.

review_improvement: Reclassifies the source-specified HMC request as gated functional automation, separates FPGA2/bus0 coverage from FPGA1/bus3 and adds decoded response/error evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: The exact same0x11/register tuple appears on a different HMC controller for FPGA1, showing that address alone cannot identify the target. This case succeeds only if bus0 is proven to represent HMC I2C-3 and the reply is decoded as FPGA2 data. A bounded transaction plus controller-specific telemetry provides that functional evidence; mandatory probing would be an unsourced change of method.
